items.content:
6 years ago I left EVERYTHING behind 👀

My old town. My school friends. My whole community. And I packed up for London. 😳 

Why?

Because the opportunities back home were limited, and so were the mindsets. It was all: good grades, uni, land a job. Nobody really backed the idea of building a business. It was "too risky." Especially at 18.

So I left.

I could barely afford rent on my tiny room share when I first started 💀 But I locked in, doubled down on my first business, and started posting online.

And shortly after, Isabella L. invited me to my first ever networking event.

That was the catalyst.

For the first time I was surrounded by ambitious people who thought like me. A whole new world of business opened up right in front of me and it lit something in me. Being around people further ahead didn't make me feel behind, it made me want to LEARN. That hunger came directly from the people I chose to put around me 🤍

Because I genuinely couldn't have built Club Peppermint without them.

From my first investor who took a chance on me, to my entrepreneur friends who push me every day. And I don't say this lightly, especially as women, because the business world still isn't an equal playing field. A circle of women who lift each other up is everything 🥹 

We went for coffee yesterday and Lara Acosta rocked up in her Peppermint jumper. 😭  Little moments like that mean more than I can explain 

It reminded me of a line from Forbes 👇

"You're the average of the five people you spend most of your time with."

The right circle raises the bar. It pushes you and helps you expect more of yourself than you would alone. Often you don't even know what you're capable of until you watch the people around you do it.

But the flip side matters just as much. Protect your energy from the people who drain it or want you to stay the same. Negativity is contagious, and you can't pour everything into building something while carrying people who want you to stay small.

And it's not just what you RECEIVE. It's what you give back. The intros, the advice, showing up for your friends. Building something isn't a solo climb, and the people who lift others as they rise are the ones who last.

Because your circle isn't just your support system.

It's your ceiling 🚀

I started posting on LinkedIn at 22 with zero clients and zero proof. The only useful thing I owned was a feed full of people already doing what I wanted.

So I started showing up in their comments, and eventually in their DMs.

Some of those DMs turned into calls. Some of those calls turned into meeting in person at a conference two years later. A few of them I now work with, travel with, or build products with.

I never stopped doing that. It's still part of my week now, with a bigger business and a lot less free time than I had at 22.

repost.content:
Model choice matters in Copilot Cowork.
⠀
$3.98. $4.77. $10.69. Same prompt. Three models. Three costs.
⠀
I ran the same task three times.
⠀
A CSV of 2025 sales figures. A PowerPoint deck. An Excel workbook. A fully interactive HTML dashboard. One prompt, three runs.
⠀
Sonnet 4.6 came back at 398 credits. $3.98.
Opus 4.8 at 477. $4.77.
GPT 5.5 at 1,069. $10.69.
⠀
GPT 5.5 was 2.7x the bill of Sonnet for the same work.
⠀
Microsoft's labels on the model picker:
⠀
- Sonnet 4.6: efficient for everyday tasks
- Opus 4.8: complex, high-stakes work
- GPT 5.5: versatile across task types
- Auto: picks for you
⠀
"Versatile across task types" sounds like the safe middle. It was the most expensive of the three by a wide margin. Worth knowing before you reach for it.
⠀
The /cost command shows you what a task spent. The model picker was the lever that decided the spend.
⠀
Reach for Sonnet on the routine work. Save the Opus runs for the complex high-stakes work that actually warrants them. Auto handles the picking when you'd rather not think about it.
⠀
Have a think about which one you're using.
